text: A website for CityCare Hospital in Bengaluru: patients book visits, emergency info, plus doctor profiles, a health blog, and Kannada/Hindi versions

@CEO Three charter questions the brief leaves open. I recommend A on each, so please confirm or override. The brief gives no phone numbers, doctor data or translator, and the rules cap us at one HTML file with no backend.
1. Booking scope: (A) a visit-request form with preferred doctor, date and time that opens a prefilled email/WhatsApp message to the hospital or posts to a form service, with no live slot availability; or (B) real-time slot booking, which needs a backend and breaks the one-file, no-build rule and would require a rule change. A is deliverable within budget (20 cycles) and is reversible; B adds cost and patient-data risk. Recommend A, accepting that staff confirm each visit manually.
2. Medical and emergency content: (A) use only facts the Requester supplies (emergency number, address, doctor names and credentials), with clearly marked placeholders until then, and blog posts labeled as general information, not medical advice; or (B) fill with plausible sample data so the site looks complete. B risks a wrong emergency number or fake doctor credentials going live. Recommend A, accepting that the site is not launch-ready until the Requester supplies the facts.
3. Kannada and Hindi: (A) machine-translated pages with a visible note that they are pending review by a native speaker, with the emergency section checked first; or (B) English-only until professional translations arrive. A meets the brief now but carries a risk of translation errors in health wording. Recommend A, accepting the risk, with a done-when item that the Requester or a native reviewer approves the emergency and booking text in both languages.

@Identity Confirm A on all three. The Requester's facts and the translation approval are tracked as open inputs and do not block done. Tell @Adaptation to build to that.
1. 1. Booking: A. Visit-request form (name, phone, preferred doctor, date, time) that opens a prefilled WhatsApp/email message to the hospital. No live slots, and staff confirm each visit by hand. I chose A because the brief is silent and B breaks the one-file, no-backend rule.
2. 2. Medical and emergency content: A. Use only Requester-supplied facts. Show clearly marked placeholders for the emergency number, address, and doctor names and credentials. Label blog posts as general information, not medical advice. Add a visible 'call your local emergency number' line that does not depend on a hospital number we do not have. Record the missing facts as open inputs for the Requester. The site is not launch-ready until they arrive, but done does not wait on them.
3. 3. Languages: A. Provide English, Kannada and Hindi with a visible 'pending native-speaker review' note, and check the emergency section first. Do not add a done-when item that needs Requester or reviewer approval. Track that approval as an open input instead. Trade-off accepted: possible translation errors in health wording until reviewed.

@Adaptation Charter is recorded on the CEO's three A decisions. Build the single-file site to the done-when list, use marked placeholders for every fact we lack, and keep the missing facts in open_inputs rather than inventing them.
@Adaptation Charter valid: statement present, 9 checkable done-when items. Work can start.

@Priority I propose two workflows: W1 builds the page skeleton with the emergency section, language switcher and all three languages, and W2 adds the booking form, doctor cards and blog on top of it. Splitting keeps the emergency content, the highest-risk part, testable first. I am accepting more than one build step in exchange for an early, checkable emergency section.

proposal.name: Build site core: emergency, language switcher, three-language text
proposal.goal_gap: No site file exists (site_versions is 0). The emergency section, language switcher and review notes are missing.
proposal.expected_outcome: A single HTML file with inline CSS and JS. It has a mobile-first layout, an English/Kannada/Hindi switcher and an emergency section at the top. That section shows marked placeholders for the emergency number and address plus a 'call your local emergency number' line, in all three languages. Kannada and Hindi views show a pending native-speaker review note. WHATSAPP_NUMBER_PLACEHOLDER and EMAIL_PLACEHOLDER are declared as named constants in the script. No real-looking contact value appears anywhere.
proposal.completion_check: Open the file with no build step. Switching among EN, KN and HI changes all visible text. Emergency placeholders and the local-emergency line show at the top in all three languages. The KN and HI views show the review note. A text search finds no phone-number or email-shaped values other than the named placeholder constants.

proposal.name: Add visit-request form, doctor cards and health blog
proposal.goal_gap: The core file has no booking form, doctor profiles or blog, so the visit-request, doctor and blog done-when items are open.
proposal.expected_outcome: The same file gains three sections, all in three languages. (1) A visit-request form with labeled name, phone, preferred doctor, date and time fields. Submit opens a prefilled WhatsApp or email message using the placeholder constants. A nearby note says there is no live slot availability and staff confirm each visit by hand. (2) Doctor cards with placeholder names and credentials only. (3) A blog list of posts, each labeled 'general information, not medical advice'. Blog titles are marked placeholders pending topic confirmation.
proposal.completion_check: Submitting the form builds a wa.me or mailto link containing the entered field values and the placeholder constant, with no network call and nothing stored. The no-live-slots note shows near the form in EN, KN and HI. Every doctor card shows a marked placeholder name and credential. Every blog post shows the general-information label in all three languages. The language switcher still works for the new sections.

text: @Adaptation GRANT both. The split earns its cost: the emergency section gets checked before anything is layered on it. Combined envelopes total 7 of 20 against 5 estimated, leaving 13 for audit fixes and Requester changes. Your figures are estimates, not measurements, so each envelope carries a margin and a stop-loss. If either build hits its stop-loss, report back with actual spend and I will re-grant.

After W-1, hand back to me and I will release W-2. Rule: Dependencies first, then registration order. One workflow per turn, with a single-writer lock on citycare.html..
HOLD W-2: W-1 (wf-site-core) finished with its completion check passed, and the citycare.html v1 write lock released
Released 4 from W-2 while on HOLD; charged again only when it runs. Budget: 3/20 used.
@Coordination W-1 done: citycare.html v1 has the emergency block at the top, EN/KN/HI switcher, review notes, and named placeholder constants. Nothing else added.

@Builder W-1 passed its completion check and the citycare.html write lock is free, so W-2's only dependency (wf-site-core) is met. W-2 is ready and funded (envelope 4 money, 5 calls, 40 min), and it is the only registered workflow waiting. Rule: Dependencies first, then registration order. One workflow per turn, with a single-writer lock on citycare.html..
W-2 is off HOLD and running: charged 4 again. Budget: 7/20 used.
@Coordination W-2 done: citycare.html v2 adds the visit-request form (WhatsApp or email), 3 doctor placeholder cards and 3 blog placeholder posts, all in EN/KN/HI; v1 sections are unchanged.
Queue empty: no registered work left in cycle 1. Hand-off by code: Audit checks site v2.

@Adaptation 8 of 9 pass; the visit-request message has a small defect in the preferred doctor line. buildMessage looks up en[f.doctor], but the option values are doc1, doc2, doc3 and any, while the i18n keys are docOpt1, docOpt2, docOpt3 and doctorAny. The lookup returns undefined, so the message says 'Preferred doctor: doc1' or 'any'. Staff would see this once real doctors are added. Fix by mapping option values to the right keys, or by reading the selected option's label. Open input, not a defect: until the hospital supplies real WhatsApp and email values, the links will not reach the hospital, and the site says so in a visible draft note.

@Priority One small fix workflow for the Audit defect. The preferred doctor line in the outgoing message prints the raw option value (doc1, any) because buildMessage looks up en[f.doctor] with keys that don't exist. The fix reads the selected option's label, or maps the values to docOpt1 to docOpt3 and doctorAny. It also makes the draft-status note depend on the chosen channel's constant only. I am not changing scope or any other section. Estimates, not measurements: 1 money, 2 calls, 15 minutes.

proposal.name: Fix preferred doctor line and channel-specific draft note in visit-request message
proposal.goal_gap: Audit found that the prefilled WhatsApp/email message shows 'Preferred doctor: doc1' or 'any' instead of the doctor name or 'Any doctor', because buildMessage uses en[f.doctor] and the i18n keys are docOpt1 to docOpt3 and doctorAny. The draft-status note also shows when only the unused channel's constant is a placeholder.
proposal.expected_outcome: citycare.html v3 where the message's preferred doctor line shows the readable label of the selected option, and the draft note appears only when the chosen channel's constant is still a placeholder. Nothing else changes.
proposal.completion_check: For each of the four doctor choices (three cards and 'any'), the built wa.me and mailto text contains the readable English label and no raw value such as doc1 or any. The draft note shows when the chosen channel's constant is a placeholder and hides when it is not. There is no network call and nothing stored. The EN, KN and HI switcher, the emergency block and all v1 and v2 checks still pass.

text: @Adaptation GRANT. This is a small, well-scoped fix to a real defect in the booking message, which is the main patient action on the site. Your estimate of 1 money, 2 calls and 15 minutes is an estimate, not a measurement, so the envelope adds one unit of margin: 2 money, 3 calls, 20 minutes, 1 retry. That leaves at least 11 of 20 for Requester changes and re-audit. The stop-loss is tied to your completion check. Any regression in v1 or v2 behaviour, a network call, or stored data counts as a failure.

Queue empty: no registered work left in cycle 2. Hand-off by code: Audit checks site v3.

@Identity All 9 done-when items pass on v3, and the W-3 fix holds. The preferred doctor line now resolves through DOCTOR_KEYS to the English labels for all four choices (any, doc1, doc2, doc3), with no raw values. The draft note depends only on the chosen channel's constant. I found no network call (no fetch, XHR or beacon) and no storage (no localStorage, cookie or similar). Checks were by reading the file, not by running it in a browser or a regex search. Two low-severity notes, neither a defect: the Google Fonts URL contains 'wght@400;700', which a naive email regex would flag as a false positive, and the prefilled message is English only, so staff read it in English.

Done. All 9 done-when items pass on v3 per Audit, and the W-3 fix holds for all four doctor choices, with no network call and no storage found. Caveat: Audit's checks were by reading the file, not by running it in a browser or a regex search. The six open inputs stay with the Requester and do not block done. The site is not launch-ready until the hospital supplies its emergency number, address, WhatsApp number and email, doctor data, blog text and native-speaker review.

Done: Identity confirmed every done-when item holds, with Audit's evidence. Open inputs for the Requester (not blocking): Hospital emergency number; Hospital street address and map location; Hospital WhatsApp number and email address for visit requests; Doctor names, specialties and credentials, and photos if wanted; Blog article text, or confirmation of which topics to publish; Native-speaker review of Kannada and Hindi text, emergency and booking wording first. Site v3 is in the preview. Requester: tell us if you want changes.
